<pr_description>
Consider the following PR description:
SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

</pr_description>

Let me analyze the issue. The problem is in `CheckboxInput.get_context()` which modifies the `attrs` dict passed to it by adding `'checked': True`. When `SplitArrayField` uses this widget in a loop, once a `True` value is encountered, all subsequent widgets also get `checked=True` because they share the same `attrs` dict.

The fix is straightforward - `CheckboxInput.get_context()` should not mutate the passed `attrs` dict. It should make a copy before modifying it.

arguments.command:
cd /testbed && cat > /tmp/fix.py << 'EOF'
import re

with open('django/forms/widgets.py', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

old = """    def get_context(self, name, value, attrs):
        if self.check_test(value):
            if attrs is None:
                attrs = {}
            attrs['checked'] = True
        return super().get_context(name, value, attrs)"""

new = """    def get_context(self, name, value, attrs):
        if self.check_test(value):
            attrs = {**(attrs or {}), 'checked': True}
        return super().get_context(name, value, attrs)"""

content = content.replace(old, new)

with open('django/forms/widgets.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
EOF
python /tmp/fix.py
